summary: Defines a media type for TimeStampedData envelopes as described in RFC 5544. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A label to stick on files that carry a trustworthy time stamp.

subtitle: The registered media type for TimeStampedData envelopes, which bind a file to time-stamp tokens.

tldr.problem: RFC 5544 defines TimeStampedData envelopes but did not register a media type for them, which limits sharing.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers application/timestamped-data, with file extension .tsd, and updates RFC 5544.
tldr.outcome: Applications can exchange TimeStampedData envelopes over MIME-based transports using a registered type. No new security considerations are introduced.

today: RFC 5955 is an Informational RFC published in August 2010. It updates RFC 5544, and no later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why a Media Type
sections.content: A TimeStampedData envelope, described in RFC 5544, binds a file with one or more time-stamp tokens obtained for that file. RFC 5544 lacked a media type registration, and the RFC says adding one enhances shareability. That is why RFC 5955 is marked as updating RFC 5544.
sections.eli5: A time-stamped file is like a photo with a date stamp. This note adds the label that tells programs what kind of file it is.

sections.title: The Registration
sections.content:
The type name is application and the subtype name is timestamped-data. There are no required or optional parameters, and the encoding is binary. The file extension is .tsd. The published specification is RFC 5544, the intended usage is COMMON, and the change controller is the IESG.

The RFC lists applications such as digital signature applications, archival systems, email clients and web browsers as ones that may exchange these envelopes.
sections.eli5: The label says: this is a binary file ending in .tsd, and many kinds of programs may handle it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security considerations of RFC 5544 apply, and this document introduces no new ones. Section 2 of the document registers a single media subtype with IANA.
sections.eli5: Adding a label does not change how safe the file is, so the old safety rules still apply.

references.text: Santoni, A., "Syntax for Binding Documents with Time-Stamps", RFC 5544, February 2010.
